_comment: Manual status overrides. Status is normally DERIVED from git — merged to
develop = done, open PR = in-review, pushed branch = in-progress. Use this
file only when reality and git genuinely disagree.
Every override needs a reason. An override without one is how a plan starts
reporting what people wish were true.
Valid status values: todo | in-progress | in-review | done | blocked

D-053.reason: Debashis — git read this as done off a branch that carried only the search half, which is why this override exists: the git evidence has been wrong since the first commit and would otherwise stay wrong. **All three halves are built and on develop (21 Aug).** Search shipped first; emoji once D-065 built the chat composer, needing no backend at all (chat_messages.body is utf8mb4, checked against the live column); file share last, merged in #266. The file-share half was recorded for months as needing a table-shape decision from Stream C. The shape chosen is a new chat_attachments table rather than a nullable ticket_attachments.ticket_id: that NOT NULL is load-bearing for C-025's scope check, C-028's delete window, C-060's cycle/stage grouping and the AV worker's claim query, and a chat file has no cycle, no stage, no client-visibility flag and no fifteen-minute window. The 'two answers to is-this-file-safe' worry is answered rather than overruled: AttachmentTypePolicy, ImageMetadataStripper and AttachmentScanner were already separate injectable beans, so chat calls the same three; only the storage key was ticket-shaped, and a StorageKey interface now covers both namespaces. Stream C's attachments package is touched in two ways, and the second is not what this note first claimed. Nine files are visibility only — package-private to public on AttachmentProperties, AttachmentScanner, AttachmentType, AttachmentTypePolicy and ImageMetadataStripper — so feature/chat can call the same beans. But AttachmentStorage's four methods also changed signature from AttachmentStorageKey to StorageKey. Callers compile unchanged and ticket attachments behave identically, because AttachmentStorageKey implements the new interface; a widened interface parameter is still an API change in another stream's package rather than a visibility tweak, and describing it as the latter undersold what was merged. Corrected here and said to Divyansh directly (issue #5, 21 Aug). That review is owed after the fact, because #266 was merged directly rather than through a batch. Verified on develop at c863007e — the migration, the six ChatAttachment* classes and ChatAttachments.tsx are all present. Closed.

D-037.reason: Debashis — git read this as done off the merge of branch feat/engines/d-037-mail-events, which was named for the task while carrying only D-030's mail body and one of the fifteen events. That is why this override exists at all: the git evidence for this task has been wrong since its first commit, and without a reason recorded here it would simply stay wrong in either direction. **All fifteen §4B.6 rows now have a producer, and all of it is on develop (21 Aug).** TicketEventNotifier wires seven — created-and-assigned (TicketWriteService, C-067), comment added (CommentService, C-029), closed (CloseService, C-040), reopened (ReopenService, C-038), reassigned-within-a-stage (AssignService, C-049), deployment-done (a forward hop out of a Deployment-owned stage, via C-045's HandoffNotifier) and sent-back-for-rework (ReworkService, C-046). Live elsewhere: handoff (HandoffNotifier, written by C-045 and deliberately left there), level raised to Critical, SLA breach, stage SLA breach, @mention and status requested. The last two rows are the digests, D-038. The fifteenth row needed a route that did not exist: nothing in the running application had ever moved a ticket backwards, so C-046's rework route was built alongside it and merged in #265. Verified on develop at c863007e — reassignedWithinStage, deploymentDone and sentBackForRework are all present in TicketEventNotifier. Closed.
